_: The future-context scenarios for 70-76 Riley Street: scripts/future_context.ts draws them over the capacity study's data. Properties are named by the start of their address as the NSW property register writes it. A building is a footprint type (single: single loaded, 12 m deep; d18: double loaded, 18 m, 8 units a floor; d22: double loaded, up to 22 m, 10 units a floor, east and west facing; consent: as approved; podium: the street wall over the whole parcel), its storeys, and the line its long axis follows: `along` a street or the party wall of a `neighbour`, `setback` metres off that line, `depth` metres deep from it (the type's depth unless smaller), `sides` off each end, `length` at most (45 m whatever is asked), kept `from` a named street's end with `endSetback` off it, or `centre`. `footprint: lot` fills the parcel. Prose may use {A.area}, {A.plate}, {A.fsr}, {A.parity}, {A.gap} and {units}. `site.tower` draws our own scheme as a podium and a tower inset from the lot by the setbacks named per street or neighbour; `site.tower.habitable` says which of its faces carry habitable rooms or balconies. A scenario's own `retained` list overrides the study's. A scenario's own `site.tower` moves our tower for that sheet.

tower._: The SSDA plans (Fuse Architects, Aug 2026): a 4-storey podium over the lot, the tower 3 m off Riley Street and Crown Lane, 3.7 m off Stanley Lane and 9 m off 66-68 Riley Street; apartments from level 2 of the podium (the ground floor commercial). `units` lays them out as the plans do, face by face from the north end, each as [number, width in metres, corner flag where the unit also has windows on that end wall]: the tower (levels 05-13 plan) 7 a floor, 3 on Crown Lane and 4 on Riley Street; the podium (level 03 plan) 10 a floor, 5 and 5, its north wall a party wall.

scenarios.title: Today
scenarios.horizon: What stands now, with our tower in it
scenarios.lead: Every building at the height the 3D tiles read for it, our tower as the model draws it: the separations and the sun the neighbours have today, and what our tower takes from them.
notes: Nothing new round the site; the storeys are the tiles' heights at 3.1 m a storey.
The sun table lists every neighbour: its apartments with two hours as it stands, and without our tower.

scenarios.title: Lot by lot
scenarios.lead: Nobody amalgamates. The two sites that already hold a consent or a lodged scheme get built, and the one clean single title on Crown Street follows as a party-wall infill.
notes: 54-56 Riley St with 1 Crown Lane ({A.area} m²) goes ahead. The 2018 scheme was 6 storeys and 16 apartments; relodged under the same logic as our site it lifts to {A.storeys} on a full-lot, single-loaded plan.
93-95 Crown St builds its approved boarding house behind the retained terrace facades.
99 Crown St, the single title south of it ({B.area} m²), takes a {B.storeys}-storey single-loaded infill between party walls.
58, 60 and 62-64 Riley St and the Crown St terraces north and south of 93-95 stay as they are. Our tower stands clearly above a mid-rise block.

scenarios.title: Paired amalgamations · north pairs
scenarios.lead: Owners of the small single titles sell together, but the strata at 62-64 Riley St and the corner terraces hold out. Two mid-size sites appear, each big enough for one slab but not for a tower.
notes: 54-60 Riley St with 1 Crown Lane become one site of {A.area} m². It takes a double-loaded 18 m slab along Yurong Lane, {A.plate}, {A.storeys} storeys, {A.gap} m off the strata to its south.

The three Crown St lots south of 93-95, with 10 Crown Lane behind them, become one site of {B.area} m². A single-loaded 12 m slab sits against the party wall of the new building at 107-113, {B.plate}, {B.storeys} storeys, every unit facing north over a {B.gap} m court.
93-95 Crown St builds its approved boarding house.
62-64 Riley St is left between two taller neighbours, which is what eventually pushes it into the full amalgamation.

scenarios.title: Paired amalgamations · the corners
scenarios.lead: The two Yurong Lane corners go first: on Riley St the DA site takes 58 with it, on Crown St the corner terrace and the lane lot behind it pair up. Everything south of them, the strata included, stays.
notes: 54-58 Riley St with 1 Crown Lane: {A.area} m², a double-loaded slab along Yurong Lane that fills the three lots, {A.plate}, {A.storeys} storeys, parity at {A.parity}.
89 Crown St with 4 Crown Lane behind it: {B.area} m², a single-loaded slab along Yurong Lane, {B.plate}, {B.storeys} storeys, every unit facing north over the lane.
93-95 Crown St builds its approved boarding house.
The new slabs stand at the far end of each block, {A.sep} and {B.sep} m from our tower: the mid-term option that touches us least.

scenarios.title: Paired amalgamations · the middle
scenarios.lead: The commercial strata at 62-64 Riley St sells with the two small titles north of it, and on Crown St the consent at 93-95 is folded into one site with the three lots south of it. These are the mid-term slabs that stand nearest our tower.
notes: 58-64 Riley St: {A.area} m², a double-loaded slab against the 66-68 party wall, {A.plate}, {A.storeys} storeys, parity at {A.parity}. Its south face stands {A.sep} m from our tower, across the retained strata: at {A.storeys} storeys the ADG asks 24 m between habitable rooms, so that face, or ours, must be blank.
93-99 Crown St with 10 Crown Lane: {B.area} m², a double-loaded slab against the 4 Crown Lane boundary, {B.plate}, {B.storeys} storeys, {B.gap} m off 105 Crown St; parity at {B.parity}.
54-56 Riley St with 1 Crown Lane, 89 Crown St with 4 Crown Lane, and 105 Crown St stay as they are.

scenarios.title: Paired amalgamations · north and south
scenarios.lead: On Riley St the four single titles north of the strata pair as before. On Crown St the block splits into two sites either side of the lane lot: the northern four with the consent bought out, the southern two against the new building at 107-113.
notes: 54-60 Riley St with 1 Crown Lane: {A.area} m², the 18 m slab along Yurong Lane, {A.plate}, {A.storeys} storeys, {A.gap} m off the strata.
89-95 Crown St with 4 Crown Lane: {B.area} m², a double-loaded slab along Yurong Lane in place of the boarding-house consent, {B.plate}, {B.storeys} storeys, parity at {B.parity}.
99-105 Crown St: {C.area} m², a single-loaded slab against the party wall of 107-113, {C.plate}, {C.storeys} storeys, every unit facing north.
62-64 Riley St, 97 Crown St and 10 Crown Lane stay: the strata between two taller neighbours, the two smallest lots between two slabs.

scenarios.title: Full amalgamation
scenarios.lead: Both groups of lots north of the retained buildings are bought out in full, including the commercial strata at 62-64 Riley St and the consent at 93-95 Crown St, and each follows our pathway to reach a density that pays for the buy-out.
notes: 54-64 Riley St with 1 Crown Lane: {A.area} m². A two-storey street-wall podium with a double-loaded 22 m tower running north-south, units facing Riley St and Crown Lane, {A.plate}, {A.storeys} storeys. Parity with our density lands at {A.parity}.

Crown St north, 89 to 105 Crown St with 4 and 10 Crown Lane: {B.area} m². A three-storey podium keeps the terrace facades on Crown St; a double-loaded 18 m tower sits across the north end, 4 m back from Crown St, {B.plate}, {B.storeys} storeys. Its smaller plate means full parity with our density would take about {B.parity}.
The towers face each other across Crown Lane, so the east tower turns its end wall to the lane. The west tower stands across the retained 2011 strata from our site boundary.
This is the upper bound: three towers of similar height between Yurong Lane and Stanley Street, with ours no longer the exception.

scenarios.title: Everything develops
scenarios.horizon: Beyond the plan, what the Commission asks us to assume
scenarios.lead: The buildings the study holds as retained go too: 66-68 Riley St joins the Riley St site, and the three new buildings on Crown St east of our lane, single titles all, make a third tower site. What matters then is the separation each tower keeps from ours, which the ADG asks of both sides.
notes: 54-68 Riley St with 1 Crown Lane: {A.area} m², the podium and 22 m tower of the full amalgamation held to the Yurong Lane end; {A.storeys} storeys, parity at {A.parity}. Its south end still stands only {A.sep} m from our tower.
Crown St north as in the full amalgamation: {B.area} m², {B.storeys} storeys.

Crown St south, 107-129: {D.area} m², 32 m deep, under the same 18 m and 2.5:1 as our site. A three-storey street wall with a double-loaded 18 m tower over it, {D.plate}, {D.gap} m off Crown Lane: {D.storeys} storeys, parity at {D.parity}. A 12 m slab facing Crown St alone would need about 21 for parity.

Across the 5.9 m lane the towers stand {D.sep} m apart. At nine storeys and over the ADG asks 24 m between habitable rooms, 18 m where one face is blank: with our east face {site.east} m off the lane their lane side must be blank, or sit {D.needs} m off the lane, which a double-loaded plate cannot afford. At 9 m each side, both face the lane freely.

Our test is the same whatever they build: 12 m off a side boundary at levels 9 and over (9 m to a lane's centreline), 9 m at 5 to 8, 6 m below. Our faces sit {site.east} m off the lane and {site.north} m off 66-68 Riley St.

scenarios.title: Separation kept, our side
scenarios.horizon: Everything develops; our tower keeps the ADG's half itself
scenarios.lead: Everything develops as there, and our tower owes nothing to its neighbours' goodwill: 9 m off Crown Lane and 9 m off 66-68 Riley St, the ADG's half at levels 9 and over. The neighbours then build the towers their sites can carry.
notes: Our tower becomes {site.plate}, {site.area} m² a floor against the {site.drawn} m² drawn, standing {site.east} m off the lane (12 m to its centreline) and {site.north} m off 66-68 Riley St.
Crown St south as in Everything develops, its tower 12 m off the lane: {D.sep} m face to face, clear of the 24 m with windows and balconies on both.
54-68 Riley St as in Everything develops, its tower at the Yurong Lane end: {A.sep} m from ours, clear.
The cost is ours, about a third of the plate; the gain is a scheme that holds whatever the Commission assumes for the neighbours.

scenarios.title: Separation kept, their side
scenarios.horizon: Everything develops; our tower stays as drawn
scenarios.lead: Our tower stays where the model puts it, {site.east} m off Crown Lane and {site.north} m off 66-68 Riley St, so the 24 m the ADG asks between towers has to be found on the neighbours' land. Each can still build, at a cost.
notes: Crown St south: with our balconies {site.east} m off the lane, a double-loaded plate cannot keep the 24 m, so the tower turns into a single-loaded 12 m slab facing Crown St, {D.plate}, {D.gap} m off the lane, its lane side a gallery. {D.sep} m face to face, clear; but {D.storeys} storeys give {D.fsr} where parity needs {D.parity}: a quarter of the site's yield gone to our setback.
54-68 Riley St: the tower {A.plate}, held to the Yurong Lane end, its south end {A.sep} m from ours, clear, at parity of {A.parity}.
Crown St north as in the full amalgamation.
This is the position the Commission is unlikely to accept: our scheme takes its separation from the neighbours' sites, and the ADG's half-to-the-boundary rule exists so that it cannot.
